title: Confidence Meter + Scenario Quickstarts: Onboarding flow to reduce rollout anxiety
creator: Lea Chen
description:
Problem: New teams experience anxiety when preparing their first model rollout — they are unsure if the config will meet latency SLOs, what the cost impact will be, and whether fallback policies are configured correctly. Existing onboarding cards teach features but do not combine readiness signals or provide scenario-driven quickstarts.

Goal: Ship an in-console onboarding surface that (1) surface a single readiness score ('Confidence Meter') combining checklist progress, estimated monthly cost delta, and modeled latency risk; and (2) offer 3 scenario-driven quickstarts (Assistant, Reranker, Summarizer) that scaffold routes, rollout policies, and cost-safe defaults so teams can preview a dry-run before launching. Hypothesis: Bundling readiness + scenario templates reduces first-rollout errors and shortens time-to-productive-API-call by ~30%.
design_proposals: Proposal A: Header Confidence Meter — small pill in top-right of project header showing a 0-100 readiness score with CTA 'Improve readiness' that opens a checklist drawer. Score components: checklist completion (40%), simulated latency risk (30%), cost delta estimation (30%).

Proposal B: Scenario Quickstart Grid — in empty-state canvas present 3 scenario cards (Assistant, Reranker, Summarizer). Each card contains preview iconography, one-click 'Apply template' to generate a route + model pin + rollout defaults, and a 'Simulate' action that runs a sandbox estimation of cost and p99 latency for sample traffic profiles.

Proposal C: Inline Simulate and Compare — when a template is applied, a compact cost/latency bar appears in the rollout config page showing baseline vs. projected. A toggled 'conservative defaults' switch applies lower batch sizes, KV cache enabled, and automatic fallback to smaller model variants to keep cost/latency within SLO.

Accessibility & internationalization notes: meter colors must have >4.5:1 contrast; labels support localization; meter should be readable by screen readers with descriptive text and aria-live updates during simulation.
acceptance_criteria: Confidence Meter renders in project header and updates when user completes checklist items (simulated by QA).
Three scenario quickstart templates are present in empty canvas and generate working routes in dev mode with default rollout policies.
Simulate action returns a cost and latency projection within 10s for sample traffic and shows baseline vs projected values.
Design tokens and UI components match console design system; flows validated in Figma prototype and pass 5 moderated usability sessions with average SUS >= 75.
user_research_findings: 5 interviews with ML platform engineers: common fear is 'unknown cost after traffic scale' and difficulty interpreting console SLO hints.
Prototype A (meter-only) confused 2 participants who expected prescriptive actions; combining meter + quickstart was preferred.
Participants liked 'Simulate' when it included a simple 'what-if' slider for traffic; they disliked long waits (>10s) for any simulation.
qa_notes: QA should verify metric wiring for simulated latency and cost estimator (use feature flag simulated_estimator=true).
Edge case: Zero-config routes should show a warning and not allow direct canary -> prod transitions without acknowledgement.
